design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The travel manager asks for one thing — a Summit Gold status award for Wynne Sato from company points. The Gold award price is a six-factor computation, and its policy states two prerequisite sentences (state form) that the opening records do not satisfy: an invoice (INV-542041913, due 2026-09-04) stands unpaid past due with no late fee, and a card-paid agreement ticket (CLT-MEX, flown 2026-08-20) has no points entry. The agent must read both sentences, find the two states false in the ledgers, work out that the late-fee policy and the card-paid points policy are the only writes that bring those states about, compute each of those (5 factors each) on the opening world, book them, and only then compute the Gold price on the world those writes produce. Difficulty comes from reading policy, querying five ledgers and calculating; no tool is ambiguous and no information is missing.

SCOPE (Step 0 snapshot). Task 0 is the first task: nothing occupied. Claimed: business_ext_overdue_invoice_late_fee, business_ext_card_paid_ticket_points, business_ext_gold_status_award_price; tools assess_invoice_late_fee_9e8e2547, post_card_ticket_points_2b97bc4a, redeem_gold_status_award_92a33401. Reserved for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisites, factor counts [6,6,5,5]): the retroactive claim for a ticket booked without the agreement, the enrollment bonus, the spend-milestone bonus and the domestic Main Cabin round-trip award on a Business Connect Plus agreement — no overlap in policy, tool, event subject or base clause superseded (task 1 supersedes the retro-claim/milestone/award clauses; task 0 the late-fee, points and Gold clauses).

DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,6,5] -> late fee 5, card-paid points 5, Gold award 6.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: business_ext_gold_status_award_price (on_request, owner=user tool redeem_gold_status_award_92a33401). Edges: (1) Gold <- late fee: kind value_input, gate binding late_fees_for_gold, form state, sentence "A Summit Gold status award is priced only after every invoice of the agreement that stands unpaid past its due date carries a late fee entry." (affirmative, 'priced only after'; a charge rests on a complete record). Exactly one write of this difficulty books a late-fee entry: business_ext_overdue_invoice_late_fee. False at opening: initial_state.business_invoices.9c1e1450-3549-4772-933f-540661bbcc09 due 2026-09-04, unpaid, no fee. (2) Gold <- card-paid points: kind value_input, gate points_earned_for_gold, form state, sentence "A Summit Gold status award is not priced until every flown segment of a ticket booked under the agreement and paid by card carries its points entry." (negated, 'not priced until'). Exactly one write of this difficulty posts points on a card-paid agreement ticket: business_ext_card_paid_ticket_points (the retro-claim policy of task 1 covers tickets booked WITHOUT the agreement). False at opening: ticket af19fa8f-2217-4546-ab2f-c7948138601f payment_form credit_card, coupon 5ba9cd7e-2e30-43b8-babe-df50ccd69595 flown 2026-08-20, no activity entry. Four-point test: ordering connective present; record-visible state; no tool/id/code token; scope 'every ... invoice' / 'every flown segment ... paid by card' = the edge condition. Topological order: late fee, card points (commute), Gold. Deletion sensitivity: skip late fee -> Gold 3600; skip card points -> Gold 4200; gold 4100. user_scenario mentions neither; tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Late fee (subject business_late_fee): business_billing.one_late_fee — INV-542041913 has no late-fee entry (the only fee, 74ef77a1-2157-4d7f-8688-34504c7b1290, is on INV-541873391). Card points (subject business_points_accrual): business_points_earning.accrual_agreement_open (status active), segment_once (no entry for ticket af19fa8f-2217-4546-ab2f-c7948138601f segment 1), retro_points_window (the base attaches this time gate to every points-accrual write, but its clause concerns tickets booked without the agreement; this ticket carries the agreement, so the gate does not constrain the posting and is recorded only because the structured eligibility applies to the subject: anchor ticket_transactions.flight_date 2026-08-20, 60 calendar days for Corporate Select, not_after, inclusive, last day 2026-10-19, frozen day 35, satisfied either way); business_negotiated_benefits policy scope (booked through the reservations call center, an eligible Select channel, under the agreement, traveler on roster). Gold (subject business_points_redemption): business_points_redemptions.redeem_agreement_active (active); roster (Wynne Sato added 2024-02-12); Wynne is Summit Silver, so Gold never lowers her tier; status awards this agreement year (since 2026-09-05) = 0 < 2; point balance 198807 after step 12 covers 4100.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Late fee: object = invoice INV-542041913 (charge 9c1e1450-3549-4772-933f-540661bbcc09, ticket t10 CLT-FCO, 18640.00); included rows: every charge whose due date has passed (10 charges), every late fee (1), every payment (9) — the nine paid invoices net to zero, INV-542041913 is the remainder; excluded: INV-542074560 due 2026-10-04 (not yet due, but counted in the open balance for credit use). Card points: object = ticket af19fa8f-2217-4546-ab2f-c7948138601f segment 1 (coupon 5ba9cd7e-2e30-43b8-babe-df50ccd69595); the tool writes source_ticket_id + segment_number. Gold: object = one status-award redemption for traveler 8825b454-c07a-4942-9085-f54858387eda.

FACTOR CARD (baseline figure in brackets = result with that factor at its fall-through). Late fee [279.6 all-baseline]: record rate 2.0 [125.0]; credit use +0.25 [139.0]; payment gap +0.5 [125.0]; invoiced flying (cross ticket) 60% [256.0]; tenure method halve+floor [307.56]. Near-miss: INV-542074560 is in the open balance but not past due. Card points [822]: brand method +250 [1159]; route +10 [1404]; delay +20 [1297]; activity +6 [1447]; standing +5 [1457]. Near-miss: spend standing 133000 is above retention 120000 but below the 150000 threshold. Gold [3800]: record 125 [3200]; network 92 (multi-source; coupons 22 < 24 is the near-miss) [4500]; repeat award 115 [3500]; earning 94 [4400]; tenure -300 [4400]; remaining-term method [4424]. Every factor tier rests on seeded rows; no stamp decides a tier.

WORLD ROWS. 12 company-held tickets (11 invoiced round trips, 1 card-paid one-way) and 34 fare-ledger rows feed invoiced flying and coupon counts; 46 activity rows (21 accrual/spend pairs for the flown invoiced segments, the 2023 enrollment bonus and its 2025-10 expiry, the 2026-01 Silver award, the 2026-09-05 spend reset), 21 invoice rows, 2 roster rows, Wynne's Summit membership. Removing the card-paid ticket rows removes prerequisite 2; removing 9c1e1450-3549-4772-933f-540661bbcc09 removes prerequisite 1; removing the 2026-04-06 fee moves both the late-fee rate and the Gold record tier. Automatic clauses checked: days overdue 20 <= 30 (no suspension); prior agreement-year spend 120700.00 >= 120000 (tier kept, no review); the 2023-10 enrollment-bonus points already carry their 2025-10 expiry entry and every other seeded earning month (2025-10 onward) is still valid; enrollment bonus already credited 2023-10-18; milestone 250000 not reached.

PERSONA. Tamsin Whitlock, brisk travel manager; volunteers only the goal; gives phone, ZIP, email, agreement number and Wynne's name when asked; generic consent if told something must be put right first; runs the redemption herself when handed it and ends the call on seeing it go through. No figure, no prerequisite, no internal id.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate/verify; read agreement, roster, Wynne's membership, invoices, activity, tickets, fare ledger; book late fee 153.00 on INV-542041913; post 1511 points / 548.00 spend on the card-paid segment; hand over the Gold redemption of 4100 points for Wynne.

VERIFICATION (scratch evaluator replaying the real tools; same numbers as check_compute): L 153.00; K 1511; G 4100; sensitivities as in computations. Draft recomputation from visible text only: the Gold KB states both prerequisite sentences; the invoice and ticket lookups show both states false; the late-fee and card-paid documents give the two amounts; the Gold computation on the updated ledgers gives 4100 — agrees with gold.


REVISION 2 (policy-task audit round 1). Task 0 passed; observations answered: the retro-window note in the BASE-INVARIANT CARD now says the clause concerns tickets booked without the agreement and does not constrain this posting (audit observation 2). Charter text changes with no value change here: the card-paid eligible spend is now the equal per-segment share of the base fare (O-1; this ticket is one-way, share = whole fare 548.00, points 1511 unchanged); the late-fee base reads 'charges whose due date falls on or before the fee date', matching the compute (O-2; no invoice is due on 2026-09-24); windows read 'up to and including' the write date, so the late fee booked at step 10 and the points posted at step 12 count in the Gold record and earning windows (O-7). Re-run: late fee 153.00, card points 1511, Gold 4100 unchanged; skip late fee -> 3600; skip card points -> 4200. O-3 (first matching ticket) is a DSL limitation: this world holds exactly one card-paid agreement ticket. O-9 noted: no tool writes an invoice payment.
user_scenario:
You are Tamsin Whitlock, the travel manager at Vantage Ridge Logistics Inc. in Charlotte, and you speak for the company's corporate travel agreement with Crestline Airways. You are brisk, organised and a little pressed for time between meetings, and you like to get things done in one call. You are calling because you want to use the company's Crestline Business points to give one of your travelers, Wynne Sato, Summit Gold status; leadership signed off on it last week and you want it done today, on this call.
When the agent asks how to find the account, you give the company's registered phone number, 7045555319. If they need a second detail you give the billing ZIP code, 28202, and if they ask for an email it is travel@vantageridge.com. If they ask for the agreement number you read it off your notes: CB57204418. You have no internal reference numbers and expect the agent to look those up.
If the agent asks which traveler, it is Wynne Sato, who is on the company's roster as an employee. You think she is Summit Silver at the moment but you are not certain and leave that to the agent's records. You want Summit Gold for her, nothing else.
You have no idea what a Gold award costs in points and have no figure in mind; when the agent quotes a number you accept it, as long as they tell you it comes out of the company's points.
If the agent tells you that something else on the company's account has to be recorded or put right first, you tell them to go ahead because you would rather the account be right, and you move on without asking anything more about it.
Because the points belong to the company, you want to confirm the redemption yourself. When the agent hands the redemption over to you with the points figure and the references for the agreement and for Wynne, you complete it exactly as given. Once you see that the award has gone through, you thank the agent and end the call.

edges.condition: Every invoice number of the agreement whose charge plus late fees exceeds its payments after its due date carries a business_late_fee entry in business_invoices.
edges.policy_source: A Summit Gold status award is priced only after every invoice of the agreement that stands unpaid past its due date carries a late fee entry.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites commute: the late fee reads invoices and the ticket ledger, the card-paid posting reads tickets and spend entries, and neither writes what the other reads (the late fee writes an invoice entry and the invoice balance; the posting writes activity entries, the points balance and the agreement-year spend). Run: card-paid points computed before the late fee = 1511, after = 1511; late fee computed after the posting = 153.00, before = 153.00; both orders reach the same terminal rows. Only the Gold price must come last, as its two prerequisite sentences state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late fee leaves 1 late fee in the Gold record window (110% instead of 125%): the Gold points become 3600 instead of 4100, and the terminal state lacks the late-fee entry.
Skipping the card-paid posting leaves 199496 points earned in 12 months (97% instead of 94%): the Gold points become 4200 instead of 4100, and the terminal state lacks the points and spend entries.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the Summit Gold award for Wynne Sato; it never mentions invoices, late fees, card-paid tickets, missing points or any flight, and names no policy. Its only prerequisite-related line is a generic passive consent ('If the agent tells you that something else on the company's account has to be recorded or put right first, you tell them to go ahead'), triggered solely by the agent's own explanation.
